Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and his wife Dimple Yadav will visit the Ram Temple and Hanumangarhi in Ayodhya on December 12, former SP MLA Pawan Pandey announced on Saturday, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections scheduled for early 2027."Both Akhilesh ji and his wife Dimple Yadav ji will visit Ram Temple and also visit the Hanumangarhi temple at Ayodhya on December 12," Pandey, who has been renominated as the SP candidate from Ayodhya, told reporters.The proposed visit will be Akhilesh's first to the Ram Temple since its inauguration in January 2024. The SP chief has faced repeated criticism from the BJP over not visiting the temple, with the ruling party accusing him of pursuing appeasement politics.Pandey said Akhilesh would visit Ayodhya with his family, meet saints and seek their blessings. The announcement comes as the BJP government led by Yogi Adityanath prepares for Deepotsav celebrations in the temple town.Akhilesh has previously said he would visit the Ram Temple after the completion of Kedareshwar Dham, a temple being built by the Samajwadi Party in Etawah.He has also accused the BJP and Sangh organisations of "chanda chori" in connection with the Ram Temple.The proposed visit comes amid the political contest over Ayodhya ahead of the 2027 polls. The BJP has repeatedly invoked the police firing on karsevaks in the 1990s, when Mulayam Singh Yadav was Uttar Pradesh chief minister, while targeting the SP.
Article Summary: Akhilesh Yadav and his wife Dimple Yadav will visit the Ram Temple and Hanumangarhi in Ayodhya on December 12. Former SP MLA Pawan Pandey announced the visit ahead of the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections scheduled for early 2027. Akhilesh has faced repeated criticism from the BJP over not visiting the temple.

Article Title: ‘Congress has not had a level playing field’: Sonia targets Modi govt amid SIR row
Article Text:
Sonia Gandhi said she was not pessimistic about the Congress party's future.

'I'm not so pessimistic'

Sonia PM on Modi, RSS and Manmohan Singh

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has alleged that her party and other opposition parties have not had a level playing field since the BJP came to power in 2014, accusing the Modi government of exercising control over key institutions, including the Election Commission In an interview with The Hindu ahead of the November 10 release of her memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", the former Congress president said the Congress had continued to fight despite what she described as institutional pressure, control over mainstream media and the use of money and religion in politics.Her remarks come amid the opposition's campaign against the Election Commission over the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The Congress-led INDIA bloc held a major rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on November 1, accusing the poll body of electoral irregularities and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The Opposition has alleged that the revision exercise could lead to eligible voters being removed from electoral rolls. The Congress has also stepped up its criticism of the Election Commission and its handling of the process.Asked about the Congress's decline, its present position and its prospects, Sonia said she was not pessimistic about the party's future. She argued that the Congress and other opposition parties had been operating under difficult conditions since the BJP came to power."I am not so pessimistic. Consider that the Congress party and other opposition parties have not had a level playing field since this government came to power. Take into account the complete stranglehold they have on all institutions, especially the Election Commission, their control of mainstream media, their money power and their exploitation of religion."She maintained that the Congress had shown resilience despite these challenges and continued to make progress."Yet, our party is fighting and making progress; in fact, it is the only party that has had the resilience to withstand this onslaught," Gandhi said.She alleged that Congress workers and leaders had faced different forms of persecution but continued to uphold the party's constitutional values."And yet, in every village and every district, Congressmen and women are still fighting for the values enshrined in our Constitution," she said.Gandhi also alleged that several elections had been manipulated and claimed that voters were increasingly aware of it."What is more, it has been amply proved in recent months that many elections have been stolen, and people are now more aware of it," she alleged. "The Congress is working with like-minded parties, and our prospects are improving day by day," she said.The Congress leader also accused the Modi government of weakening India's democratic institutions over the past 12 years, warning that rebuilding them would take considerable time even after a change in government."Over the last twelve years great damage has been done to the fabric of our country, our democracy and our institutions. Even after this government goes, it will take time to restore our systems back to health and great effort from political parties," she said.However, she expressed confidence that people would support a return to what she described as proper governance."But I am optimistic and I know that the people of India will welcome a return to proper governance," the former Congress chief said.Asked what the Congress could learn from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's political rise, Gandhi said his ideological background was different from that of the Congress but dismissed the need for the party to draw lessons from the RSS."It's true that he comes from a very different ideological world. But there are many ways that people succeed in politics within the Congress party, take for example Dr. Manmohan Singh and Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge. I don't think we have much to learn from the RSS."She also rejected the suggestion that she had ever reconsidered her decision to decline the prime minister's post after the Congress-led alliance won the 2004 general election."No, not at all. That has never crossed my mind. Our experience was by and large a very positive one. We worked as a team, and our roles were distinct, with him (Singh) leading the government and I leading the party."Gandhi's 544-page memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", is scheduled to be released in India by HarperCollins India on November 10. The book is primarily a personal account of her life, with political events forming the backdrop to her journey.
Article Summary: Sonia Gandhi says she is not pessimistic about the Congress party's future. She accuses the Modi government of exercising control over key institutions, including the Election Commission. The former Congress president said the Congress had continued to fight despite institutional pressure, control over mainstream media and use of money and religion in politics.

Article Title: 'More you connect with locals, weaker enemy’s plots become': Rajnath Singh's message to troops in WB's Bagdogra

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday addressed soldiers in West Bengal's Bagdogra and advised them to build a deeper connect with local residents in sensitive border areas."The more you connect with local people, the weaker the enemy's plots will become," news agency ANI quoted him as saying."At the post where you serve, your conduct, your uniform, your language and your restraint shape the army's image in the minds of local people. The people of Bagdogra and the surrounding areas have great affection for the army. It is also your responsibility to preserve that affection," he said.Singh underlined the need for discipline and courage, calling them vital qualities for every soldier in the armed forces."No matter how advanced technology is, if our soldiers lack discipline and courage, it is useless. Our armed forces are known for their discipline. Discipline is what transforms an ordinary soldier into an extraordinary warrior. Your discipline is your greatest strength," he said."Among the challenges we face today, morale is the greatest weapon. When your morale is high, you can achieve great victories even with a small team.How does morale grow? Morale grows when you know that your country is with you, your leadership is with you," he added.Bagdogra lies near the strategically significant Siliguri Corridor , popularly known as the 'Chicken's Neck', a narrow strip of land in northern West Bengal that connects mainland India to the northeastern states. The corridor is also in close proximity to the international borders with China, Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh.

NEW DELHI: Senior advocate Kapil Sibal on Saturday questioned the government's changing stand on holding a discussion on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Parliament, suggesting that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi sit together for an open debate on the issue."Earlier, when the Opposition demanded a discussion on SIR, the Home Minister said the government had nothing to do with it as it was the Election Commission's responsibility. Now, he is saying that a special session can be convened for a discussion. Why has the government's stand changed? I have a suggestion: let the Prime Minister and the Leader of Opposition sit together and question each other. Let the discussion continue as long as possible. This would give the Prime Minister an opportunity to answer questions for the first time in 12 years, which would be a historic occasion," Sibal said.His remarks came after Rahul Gandhi on Saturday challenged Union Home Minister Amit Shah to an open debate on the SIR exercise. Sharing a video of Shah's remarks, the Congress leader said, "Amit Shah ji, don't confuse Modi ji. Just convince him to have an open debate with me.Any platform, any time. Don't be afraid."The challenge drew a sharp response from the BJP, with Parliamentary Affairs Minister Pralhad Joshi accusing Rahul of sharing an edited video of Shah's remarks without the proper context. He said the clip exposed Rahul's "absolute lack of homework on SIR".The video featured Shah's remarks in Parliament and at another public address. In his parliamentary remarks, Shah questioned the possibility of holding a discussion on SIR in the House and asked who would be held responsible if questions were raised.Responding to Rahul's demand for a debate with the Prime Minister, Shah said Modi's presence was not necessary for the discussion."Rahul ji, Modi ji ki zaroorat nahi hai... It ended with Rahul smiling at a press conference, alongside an overlay reading "Confusion mein aa gaye".

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Saturday rejected claims of excessive ethanol blending in petrol at certain retail outlets in Karnataka, saying all 56 samples tested in the state under a nationwide quality monitoring exercise complied with prescribed E20 specifications.The ministry of petroleum and natural gas (MoPNG) said the three public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs) — Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL), Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd (HPCL) — had clarified that reports of 26-31 per cent ethanol blending were not supported by tests conducted under prescribed statutory and technical procedures.According to the ministry, E20 petrol supplied by the three companies across the country, including Karnataka, conforms to IS 17021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for ethanol-blended motor gasoline.The ministry said 893 samples collected across 27 states and Union territories were found compliant with the prescribed quality standards. All 56 samples tested in Karnataka also met the specifications, with ethanol content ranging from 19 per cent to 20 per cent.The OMCs, however, raised concerns over the sampling procedure and testing methodology adopted during an October 2026 exercise in Karnataka. They sought joint sampling and independent testing under prescribed standards to verify the reported ethanol levels."The Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply, Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 2005, issued under the Essential Commodities Act, 1955, read with the Marketing Discipline Guidelines (MDG) 2024, prescribes a defined procedure for sampling, retention, testing and communication of results," the ministry said.Under the prescribed procedure, six one-litre samples are to be drawn. Two are handed over to the dealer, two retained by the oil company or department, and the remaining two sent to a designated laboratory for testing.The government also said samples collected during a September 2026 exercise were routed through the state level coordinator to designated OMC laboratories and tested for the required quality parameters.The Centre for High Technology (CHT), under the ministry of petroleum and natural gas, has been continuously monitoring ethanol blending and fuel quality at OMC retail outlets, the ministry added.
Article Summary: The Centre on Saturday rejected claims of excessive ethanol blending in petrol at certain retail outlets in Karnataka. All 56 samples tested in the state under a nationwide quality monitoring exercise complied with prescribed E20 specifications. According to the ministry, E20 petrol supplied by the three companies across the country, including Karnataka, conforms to IS 17021.

NEW DELHI: Union railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Saturday said the Railways has deployed 18,000 special trains this festive season to manage the rush during Durga Puja, Diwali and Chhath, up from 12,000 operated last year.Vaishnaw said holding areas have been set up at around 20 railway stations to help passengers wait comfortably for their trains. Ticket counters have also been shifted from station premises to these areas, while additional scanning counters have been installed to speed up security checks and prevent long queues.The Railways has also installed around 700 AI-enabled cameras as part of its crowd-management measures, he said.“Special trains have been stationed at various locations, including Shakur Basti, Nizamuddin, Anand Vihar, Anand Vihar Terminal, and near New Delhi station,” Vaishnaw said.He added that the Railways operated around 75,000 special trains in the previous financial year, with the number expected to cross 80,000 this year.Referring to the situation on Chhoti Diwali, the minister said passenger movement and traffic at railway stations had returned to normal.“Even today, on the occasion of Chhoti Diwali, the traffic situation across all locations has already returned to normal. We intend to maintain this throughout the festive season,” he said.While speaking on train delays, network congestion, freight movement, and long-term capacity expansion projects, Vaishnaw said, "We are currently experiencing a period of peak congestion. There is a peak in the movement of coal and other goods. To address this, 36,000 kilometres of additional tracks have been laid over the last 10 years. Constructing new tracks and increasing capacity is crucial; this is the only way to provide a permanent solution. We must continue to build more tracks."
Article Summary: Railways has deployed 18,000 special trains this festive season to manage the rush during Durga Puja, Diwali and Chhath. Vaishnaw said holding areas have been set up at around 20 railway stations to help passengers wait comfortably for their trains.

NEW DELHI: Referring to the contradictory orders given by Supreme Court in the matter of bail to the accused on the ground of delay in trial and long incarceration for UAPA offences, which have been referred to a larger bench for authoritative pronouncement, former student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved SC for bail in 2020 Delhi riots cases.The accused submitted that two co-accused, including Tasleem Ahmed, were granted bail by SC on the grou-nd that determination of the issues by the larger bench would take time, and they could not be made to suffer continued incarceration.Seeking parity with the co-accused, Sharjeel Imam, who has already spent six years and nine months in custody, said in his petition, filed through advocate Fauzia Shakil, that two co-accused in the same FIR were released on interim bail by the court on May 22 under a principle which applies to him in greater degree.The accused moved SC after their plea for bail was rejected by the trial court and Delhi High Court on the ground that the apex court had purportedly set a deadline of Jan 5, 2027, for them to file a bail petition.The petition asked "whether the principle recognised by this Court in Tasleem Ahmed v. State order dated 22.05.2026, that an accused cannot be made to suffer continued incarceration merely because an important question of law has arisen for authoritative settlement, can be withheld from the petitioner alone by reference to the role attributed to him, when the question referred to concerns the correctness of the very judgment which declined his bail and relief in Tasleem Ahmed case was granted without any examination of role?"It further argued, "Whether liberty reserved by this Court in a judgment declining bail, to renew the prayer for bail at a defined point, operates as a bar upon the statutory jurisdiction of the Special Court and of the High Court to consider an application for bail founded on supervening circumstances be-fore that point, when the same paragraph of the judgment holds that pre-trial detention cannot be permitted to continue without regard to the progress of the trial and that Article 21 operates as a continuing check against continued incarceration without substantial progress of the trial?"
Article Summary: Former student activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have moved SC for bail in 2020 Delhi riots cases. The accused submitted that two co-accused, including Tasleem Ahmed, were granted bail by SC on the grou-nd that determination of the issues by the larger bench would take time.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Friday said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations, asserting that President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback.Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram, Tharoor said the US election results would not change Washington's approach towards key issues such as tariffs, sanctions on countries buying Russian oil, the Iran war or the Ukraine conflict."Whether it comes to tariffs, whether it comes to sanctions for buying Russian oil, whether it comes to the Iran war itself, whether it comes to any initiative he takes on the Ukraine war. All of this, he's completely unaffected by the election result," Tharoor said.He explained that while Congress has significant powers over budgetary matters and can restrict or approve government spending, the President enjoys considerable discretion in foreign policy and international affairs.Tharoor said that even when it comes to military action, the President can proceed without seeking approval for an initial period of up to 60 days. However, Congress can exercise its financial powers to restrict expenditure, particularly in the case of an expensive military campaign."Those in India who are expecting this to have some impact on our relationship with the US, I think, are completely mistaken," he said.Commenting on the election outcome, Tharoor described it as an extraordinary setback for the ruling party, pointing out that midterm elections traditionally serve as a course correction for the party in power.He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin, including the election of a mayor of Indian origin in Los Angeles.Tharoor said the results reflected the vibrancy of American democracy but maintained that the outcome would not significantly alter Trump's ability to take decisions on international affairs.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations. He said President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback. He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin.

NEW DELHI: Indian Youth Congress has suspended over 300 office-bearers from the organisation for not showing up for the 'Chalo Delhi' rally of INDIA bloc Sunday - a significant step to drive home the message that the outfit is serious about mass mobilisation in future.IYC sources said organisational office-bearers from assembly to the central level were directed to attend the rally with Rahul Gandhi as the face. NEW DELHI: NCP leader Praful Patel on Thursday visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital and enquired about his health. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups.The visit by Patel has triggered political speculation as he is among the NCP leaders reportedly "unhappy" with party boss Sunetra Pawar’s leadership. The meeting comes amid signs of internal discord within the party, adding a political dimension to Patel’s hospital visit.Sharad Pawar was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital on Wednesday night with a respiratory and chest infection, after being discharged from Pune’s Ruby Hall Clinic. Dr Pratit Samdani, a doctor at the hospital, said on Thursday that Pawar was stable and undergoing treatment."Sharad Pawar was admitted yesterday at Breach Candy Hospital for a respiratory and chest infection. He is stable and under treatment. He was admitted last night; he had a cough and an infection, something like bronchitis trouble. His treatment is ongoing, and he is currently stable," Dr Samdani told reporters.After meeting Pawar, Patel said the hospital admission was part of his routine medical check-ups and that his health was good. He also dismissed speculation that their meeting involved political discussions, saying he continued to meet Pawar and his daughter, Supriya Sule, because of their family ties.Also read: Rest, Supriya and I’ll look after country, PM Narendra Modi said to have told Sharad Pawar In a post on X, Patel said, "I visited the Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai to pay a courtesy call on the esteemed Shri Sharad Pawar Saheb and inquired about his health."Providing an update on Pawar's condition, Patel said, "Sharad Pawar due to fatigue two days ago, was taken to Ruby Hall Clinic in Pune for a checkup. After that, he came to Mumbai, and here his health is fine. Naturally, a checkup happens once or twice a year, for a complete checkup, so in that context only he is admitted here at Breach Candy. His health is good. I am also happy that I came here, but everything is fine, and sahab was also in good spirits. He was asking about what is happening in politics in the country and state, as that is his interest. We had a good conversation, and I am happy that in a day or two all his checkups will be completed, so he will return home soon so he can rest."Patel also commented on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's conversation with Pawar, describing their relationship as long-standing and cordial. He said Modi's call to enquire about Pawar's health was natural given their association over the years.“Sharad Pawar and Narendra Modi have had a very long-standing relationship. I have also known Modi ji for many years and personally know about the relationship between him and Pawar sahab... I have witnessed their very good, cordial and respectful relationship over the years, even when we were in the UPA government in Delhi, and Modi ji was the Chief Minister of Gujarat... Modi ji is such a senior leader of the country today. So, if he received information about Sharad Pawar ji's health, it was natural for him to enquire about his well-being and speak to him...”Earlier, Pawar was admitted to Ruby Hall Clinic on November 2 after complaining of a cough and pleuritic chest pain. According to a statement issued by Dr Purvez K Grant, Chief Cardiologist, Chairman and Managing Trustee of the hospital, Pawar was stable and doing well at the time of his discharge."Mr Sharad Pawar has been discharged from Ruby Hall Clinic today. He is stable and doing well. He will be travelling directly from the hospital to his residence in Mumbai. We wish him good health and a speedy recovery," the statement said.His daughter, Baramati MP and NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule, had earlier said that Pawar was undergoing medical tests and that his health parameters were stable. Ruby Hall Clinic subsequently said he would remain under observation as a precautionary measure. Doctors cleared him for discharge after his condition remained stable and his discomfort subsided.The developments come amid growing concerns within the BJP over organisational differences in its ally -- NCP. Union home minister Amit Shah met several senior NCP functionaries late Sunday who are believed to be unhappy with party president Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, and urged them to resolve their differences in the party’s interest.Those who met Shah included NCP national working president Praful Patel, Maharashtra unit chief Sunil Tatkare, ministers Chhagan Bhujbal and Hasan Mushrif, and leaders Dhananjay Munde and Dilip Patil. Deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth were absent from the meeting.Following the meeting, Sunetra Pawar convened a core committee meeting in Mumbai.
Article Summary: NCP leader Praful Patel visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups. The visit by Patel has triggered political speculation as he is among the NCP leaders reportedly "unhappy" with party boss Sunetra Pawar's leadership.

Article Title: Centre eases immigration rules for Pakistani, Afghan minorities and other foreign nationals

NEW DELHI: The Union home ministry has relaxed passport and visa requirements for several categories of foreign nationals residing in India, including Pakistani citizens who entered prior to December 31, 2009 with the intention to permanently reside in India but could not renew their Pakistani passport due to non-possession of computerised nationality identity card issued by Pakistan government.Other categories of foreign nationals for whom passport and visa rules have been eased as part of the Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) (Amendment) ORder, 2026, include citizens of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan belonging to their religious minorities; Sri Lankan Tamil refugees and Tibetans.The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan, allowing them to enter or exit India by producing any one of the documents specified in the visa manual; However, in case they are entering or exiting India from or to a place other than Nepal or Bhutan, they must in possession of a valid passport. Nepal and Bhutan citizens who have embarked at or transited through China Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan, must be in possession of both a valid passport and valid visa.The requirement of a valid passport and visa would also not apply to a male member of the Muslim community, being originally an Indian citizen, who went to Pakistan after partition between August 15, 1947 and Dec 31, 1965 leaving behind family in India and returned to India on or before Dec 31, 2009, and settled in Keralam on a valid Pakistani passport but which has since expired or been lost.However, such a person should not have married or acquired immoveable property while in Pakistan; ,while going to Pakistan, left behind family members who are Indian citizens; shall not return to Pakistan; and should not have any adverse report from the police or security agencies.A citizen of India entering into India from Nepal or Bhutan or departing from India to Nepal or Bhutan by land or air shall produce before the immigration officer one of the documents specified in the visa manual to establish their identity, though this exemption would not be applicable if departing to or returning from countries other than Nepal or Bhutan through the Indo-Nepal or Indo-Bhutan border of by air. In all such cases, a valid passport will be required and the exit and entry into India shall be only through the designated immigration points.The provisions in the Act and rules with regard to requirement of valid passport or other valid travel document and valid visa for entry into, stay in and exit from India, shall also not apply for a member of naval, military or air forces of India, entering into or exiting from India on duty and members of the family of any such person when accompanying him on a government transport; registered Sri Lankan Tamil nationals who have taken shelter in India up to Jan 9, 2015; as well as the foreign crew of foreign military vessels coming for repairs in India who are granted military ship repair permits by the immigration officer, provided they hold their military identification documents.Exempted categories include a Tibetan who has entered India after 1959 but before May 30,, 2003 on an entry permit issued by the Embassy of India in Kathmandu; or who entered after May 30, 2003, on the special entry permit issued through the designated immigration post on the Indo-Nepal border and a certificate of registration was issued by the registration officer concerned.Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Christian, Jain and Parsi citizens of Pakistan who entered India before Dec 31, 2024, fearing religious persecution in their home country, without valid documents including passport or other travel documents; or with valid documents including passport that has since expired, would also get relief under the amended Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) order. However, such a person shall be required to obtain an appropriate category of visa after their entry into India, for continued stay.Also exempt now from requirement of a valid passport and visa are persons of Indian origin who subsequently acquired the citizenship of Malaysia or Singapore and returned to India on or before Dec 31, 2009 on a valid passport issued by either of those countries, which has since expired and is not being renewed by those countries because such person does not meet the conditions specified by those countries. Such persons must have documentary proof that they are a person of Indian origin.
Article Summary: The order also streamlines travel and identification protocols for the citizens of Nepal and Bhutan. Pakistani citizens who entered prior to December 31, 2009 could not renew their Pakistani passport due to non-possession of computerised nationality identity card. Other categories of foreign nationals for whom passport and visa rules have been eased include citizens of Pakistan, Afghanistan and Pakistan belonging to their religious minorities.

NEW DELHI: Electors across seven states/UTs undergoing SIR, including Delhi, who were excluded from the draft electoral roll on account of being absent, shifted, dead or duplicate (ASDD) and whose enumeration forms (EFs) were not received, will be provided one more opportunity to get their names included in the final electoral roll by filling up the SIR form afresh. They will no longer have to fill Form 6, meant for fresh enrolment, or Form 8, if they were excluded due to shifting of place of residence within the same state/UT.The drive in states where SIR is under way - Delhi, Haryana, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana and Nagaland - may come as a relief for deleted electors who were reluctant to fill Form 6 to be added back, in view of the declaration in the form that they were enrolling for the first time. "Basically, the enumeration window which stopped with the publication of draft roll is being reopened for the deleted ASDD voters till the end of the claims and objections period," an EC official said.EC, in a letter to chief electoral officers of the above states/UT, said ASDD electors may submit their EF physically or online to the electoral registration officer or booth-level officer (BLO), along with an annexure mentioning the reason why they could not submit it earlier and declaring that they have not submitted Form 6 for fresh enrolment during SIR.An elector who was excluded due to shifting of residence within the same state/UT can submit the EF along with an annexure mentioning why it was not submitted earlier and declaring that they have not submitted Form 6 during SIR. In the annexure, such voters must mention the address where they were enrolled earlier as well as the address to which they have now shifted. Residence proof will need to be attached.The EF, along with the annexure, must be submitted to the ERO of the assembly constituency to which the voter has shifted. The poll panel said partially filled EFs of left-out ASDD electors will be generated afresh in the ERO dashboard in ECINet. The district election officer and ERO shall make all efforts to contact such electors through BLOs.The district election officer and ERO shall ensure delivery of EFs either physically or electronically via WhatsApp, SMS or email where contact details are available. Affected electors can download and fill up EF on ECINet with their old EPIC number.Booth-wise lists of such ASDD voters will be displayed afresh on notice boards and also uploaded on the CEO's website.EC directed BLOs to get in touch with electors marked as ASDD through house-to-house visits; enquiries from neighbours, family members, RWAs and by using available contact numbers.EFs received from such electors shall be processed and disposed of by EROs concerned after verification of the applicant's eligibility, ordinary residence as well as field verification.Once approved, the same EPIC number assigned to the elector prior to SIR shall be re-assigned. An elector who has already submitted Form 6 for fresh enrolment during SIR need not submit the enumeration form with statement afresh.
Article Summary: Electors excluded from draft electoral roll will be given one more opportunity to get their names included in final electoral roll. They will no longer have to fill Form 6, meant for fresh enrolment, or Form 8, if they were excluded due to shifting of place of residence within state/UT.

Article Title: Ailing Kerala elephant calf, Maya, airlifted to Anant Ambani's Vantara for intensive hospitalisation
Article Text:
A crucial second opinion brings renewed hope

A collaborative model of compassionate care

Maya, an 18-month-old critically ill orphaned elephant calf, has been airlifted from Kerala’s Abhayaranyam to Anant Ambani's Vantara in Jamnagar for specialised intensive hospitalisation. The calf, who has been unable to stand following a severe fall in July, was shifted to the facility after medical experts sought advanced veterinary intervention as a final effort to prevent euthanasia. This life-saving transfer was initiated when Kerala officials explicitly requested the intervention of Vantara to explore every possible medical avenue.Maya's short life has already been a test of resilience. On April 19, 2025, she was found abandoned as a severely dehydrated newborn near Kaprikkad in the Malayattoor Division. Rescued and brought to Abhayaranyam, she was hand-reared around the clock by the Kerala Forest Department. Sadly, her struggles did not end there. On July 2, 2026, the calf slipped while playing and injured her right shoulder. Despite physiotherapy and dietary supplements, her condition rapidly deteriorated.By late October, she could no longer stand and was accepting only liquid feed. A thorough external examination revealed multiple fractures in her limbs, a chest infection, and generalised bone thinning. Faced with extremely brittle bones and a grave prognosis, a Medical Board made the heavy animal-welfare decision to recommend euthanasia on October 29 to prevent further suffering.Refusing to close the case, Kerala’s Chief Wildlife Warden, Dr. P. Pugazhendi, pursued a wider expert opinion before considering any irreversible actions. After reviewing her X-rays and blood work during a video consultation, Vantara’s veterinary experts identified a potential parathyroid-related disorder that could respond to treatment. With this new possibility, the decision was unanimously made on November 5 to transfer Maya to Vantara. At their facility, she will receive comprehensive pain management, advanced diagnostics, and support from hydraulic lifting systems to position her safely. Stepping in to provide this critical care, Vantara acted on the core principle of Anant Ambani: every life matters, driven by the philosophy of Jeev Seva.What makes this medical mission truly remarkable is the deep partnership built around the calf's emotional well-being. Before the journey, Vantara submitted a comprehensive treatment plan, and arranged an airlift equipped with life-support systems. To ensure Maya feels secure in an unfamiliar environment, the Kerala Forest Department has sent Assistant Forest Veterinary Officer Dr. Binoy C. Babu and her familiar caregiver, Shri Nikhil Babu, to accompany her on the flight.Crucially, her caregiver will remain by her side throughout the entire treatment period in Jamnagar to provide vital continuity. A Kerala Monitoring Committee will closely oversee her medical progress, and once the treatment is complete, Vantara will facilitate her return home to Abhayaranyam.The road ahead is undeniably difficult, and her prognosis remains uncertain. However, with two dedicated institutions working flawlessly together and familiar faces by her side, every conceivable effort is being made to give Maya the best possible chance.
Article Summary: Maya, an 18-month-old critically ill orphaned elephant calf, has been airlifted from Kerala’s Abhayaranyam to Anant Ambani's Vantara in Jamnagar. The calf, who has been unable to stand following a severe fall in July, was shifted to the facility after medical experts sought advanced veterinary intervention to prevent euthanasia.

Article Title: Ousted Videocon promoter Dhoot declared bankrupt over dues worth Rs 12,668cr
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: From a Bajaj Auto dealership in Maharashtra to one of the largest consumer durable companies in the country, life has come full circle for Videocon Industries' ousted promoter Venugopal Dhoot who was declared bankrupt by National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) a day before Dhanteras, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.Dhoot is one of the most high-profile individuals to be declared bankrupt under the decade-old Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code , with the Mumbai bench of NCLT directing him to file his statement of financial position within seven days with the bankruptcy trustee Asish Narayan, who will manage his estate.A bench of judicial member Vinay Goel and technical member Charanjeet Singh Gulati declared Dhoot bankrupt over dues of Rs 12,668 crore, including interest and penalty, as he had given a personal guarantee for credit facilities extended to Videocon Industries and borrowings connected with Videocon Telecommunications. The petition was filed by State Bank of India."We are satisfied that the petition complies with all the requirements prescribed in Section 123 of the Code. Therefore, we consider it proper to admit this petition and pass the following orders: Venugopal Nandlal Dhoot, the personal guarantor herein, is declared as bankrupt," the tribunal said in its order.The bankruptcy trustee will issue a public notice inviting claims from creditors.The trustee will also handle administration and distribution of the estate.The development is bad news for promoters who had availed loans based on personal guarantees, a norm for corporate loans in the last three decades, but subsequently lost control over their companies as IBC was used for repeated defaults in repayment of dues.While provisions related to personal guarantors were notified in Dec 2019, till last June, close to 5,200 applications had been filed for initiation of personal insolvency of which 5,135 were filed with NCLT and the remaining 51 went to debt recovery tribunals. Of the 64 cases that have been approved, the repayment plans have yielded Rs 234 crore -- 1% of the admitted claims, official data showed.Unlike corporate insolvency, where a resolution professional is appointed by NCLT when the case is admitted and a resolution entity then takes over the company, in case of personal bankruptcies, the guarantor has to prepare a repayment plan, which needs to be approved by the tribunal.
Article Summary: Venugopal Dhoot is one of the most high-profile individuals to be declared bankrupt under the decade-old Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code. The Mumbai bench of NCLT directed him to file his statement of financial position within seven days with the bankruptcy trustee Asish Narayan.

Article Title: PM Modi's Sule message to Sharad Pawar; 'internal tussle' in NCP: Is Maharashtra politics heading for another churn?
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Is a storm brewing in Maharashtra’s Pawar clan? The family that saw a vertical split in 2023, seems to be at a crossroads again."As a member of the Pawar family and their relative, I want to alert Parth Pawar, Jay Pawar and Sunetra. They need to understand the political strategies of the BJP and certain leaders close to them": Nephew Rohit Rajendra Pawar’s warning for his “” Sunetra Pawar, who is the wife of late Ajit Pawar , and her two children.Sunetra, who is the deputy chief minister in the ruling BJP-led Mahayuti at present, is on the other side of the family divide. She and her sons control the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP), which was originally formed by Sharad Pawar in 1999 but was wrested from him by Ajit Pawar in 2023.So, let’s look at some of the recent developments to analyse if Rohit Pawar ’s warning has a genuine basis.Senior NCP leaders met Union home minister Amit Shah recently. Some reports suggested that the NCP leaders complained to Amit Shah about the unilateral functioning of party MP Parth Pawar and a lack of proper coordination. The NCP spokesperson denied this claim and slammed irresponsible media reporting.NCP chief Sunetra Pawar convened an urgent meeting of the core committee at her official residence, Devgiri. This was the second meeting of the core committee in a week. The first meeting happened after the senior leaders had met Amit Shah.At the core committee meeting, the party legislators and ministers expressed serious concerns over internal frictions and claimed the party is weakening in the absence of unity.Also read: Miffed with Parth, NCP seniors eager to revive merger talks with Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP); surprised, says Rohit When Sharad Pawar was hospitalised, Prime Minister Narendra Modi called him in the hospital and requested the veteran politician to prioritise his health and rest. PM Modi’s message to the senior Pawar, "Supriya and we will handle the country. You take care of your health and rest. Let your blessings remain with us," sparked political buzz. And perhaps carried a political undertone about possible churn, amid speculation about Sunetra Pawar and her sons' political future.Adding fuel to the fire, Union minister and Republican Party of India (Athawale) president Ramdas Athawale claimed that Sule could be considered for a position in the Union cabinet during its next expansion if she joined the ruling NDA.These four developments, significant in their own ways, collectively point to the flux within the NCP factions after the party was split in 2023.Ajit Pawar, while he was alive, had managed a firm grip on his faction winning 41 assembly seats in the 2024 assembly elections. There were even talks of the two factions uniting again. However, his unfortunate death in a helicopter crash in January 2026, suddenly made the NCP vulnerable and the merger talks were put to rest.Ajit’s wife Sunetra Pawar, who took over the reins of the NCP and also became a minister in the Mahayuti government, tried to fill the vacuum in the party.Her sons - Parth and Jay Pawar - became an integral part of decision-making. Senior NCP leaders who had worked with Ajit Pawar over the years were sidelined. This led to heartburn and talks of discontent within the party. It is in this context that the meeting of senior NCP leaders with Amit Shah and the subsequent meeting of the party’s core committee held by Sunetra Pawar have set tongues wagging.Rohit Pawar in his warning message had pointed to the “political strategies of the BJP and certain leaders close to them.” So, is something happening behind the scenes? Is the BJP working to merge the NCP factions to water down the influence of Sunetra and her sons?Well, there is no definitive answer to these questions.For the record, the NCP has denied all speculations of any power tussle within the party.NCP spokesperson Umesh Patil termed the reports suggesting senior party functionaries met Shah, a BJP leader, in New Delhi three days ago without informing Sunetra Pawar as "completely incorrect".Patil maintained she herself had requested the Union minister to give time to a delegation of senior party leaders. He said Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth had met Shah twice last month when discussions were held on matters related to the party, a BJP ally and constituent of the Mahayuti government in the state.Sunetra Pawar had then requested Shah to meet senior NCP leaders who had been involved in discussions with BJP leaders when the party joined the NDA, said Patil.An appointment with Shah for the delegation was subsequently given, said the spokesperson, adding the NCP's core committee and legislative wing meetings were also scheduled several days in advance.The official spokesperson also defended the involvement of Parth Pawar in party affairs, saying the Pawar family had dedicated itself to the organisation following the death of former NCP president Ajit Pawar in an air crash in January this year."After Ajit Dada's death, Sunetra Pawar (and her sons) Parth and Jay have dedicated themselves to the party," Umesh Patil said.Now, coming to the second aspect of the developments. It is not for the first time that the Prime Minister has expressed his special bond with Sharad Pawar, despite the two leaders being on opposite sides of the political divide.In July this year, Sharad Pawar and Supriya Sule met the Prime Minister at his office even as opposition MPs protested outside. The Prime Minister was then seen receiving Pawar at the door of his room. During the meeting Sharad Pawar submitted a memorandum to the Prime Minister listing the issues faced by the farmers in the country and issues related to irrigation.In February 2025, PM Modi made a gesture of respect by helping 84-year-old Sharad Pawar with his chair on stage and offering him a glass of water.In August 2023, Sharad Pawar shared the stage with PM Modi in Pune when the Prime Minister was conferred with the Lokmanya Tilak Award. The move created unease among some members of the opposition INDIA alliance. Uddhav Thackeray’s Shiv Sena (UBT) questioned the optics of the two leaders appearing together, especially when Sharad Pawar was a key leader of the opposition’s INDIA bloc.Well, the saffron party is obviously not ‘working’ or ‘not working’ to facilitate a '' reconciliation moment for the Pawar clan. The real prize of the BJP would be co-opting the political infrastructure of the veteran, who was also known as '' (people's king). With decades of work, the influence of Pawar Saheb extends beyond assembly seats to an entrenched network of sugar cooperatives, district banks, local bodies and influential political families across western Maharashtra. Though the seats and power is not transferable as it is, a working understanding with Sharad Pawar could give the BJP access to this ecosystem without having to build its own grassroots machinery from scratch.If Sharad Pawar does decide to merge and if Athawale’s claim turns out to be true, Sule may get an opportunity to be in “power” again.There may also be a larger opposition calculation at play. Sharad Pawar was instrumental in stitching together the Maha Vikas Aghadi and managing the competing ambitions of the Congress and Uddhav Thackeray's Shiv Sena. Any rapprochement with the BJP, even without a formal merger, could weaken this arrangement, complicate seat-sharing and disrupt opposition coordination in Maharashtra. The BJP could gain not just an ally but also greater room to manoeuvre against a much fragmented opposition.This will also help the BJP in Maharashtra to keep the Eknath Shinde Shiv Sena in check. The recent loss of the ruling Mahayuti in the MLC elections turned into an ugly war of words between the two allies - with the BJP accusing the Shinde Sena of not working for the coalition.A united NCP on its side may perhaps provide the BJP manoeuvring room against the Shinde Sena in Maharashtra.
Article Summary: Nephew Rohit Rajendra Pawar has warned his family about the political strategies of the BJP and certain leaders close to them. Sunetra Pawar, who is the wife of late Ajit Pawar and her two children, is on the other side of the family divide. She and her sons control the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP), which was originally formed by Sharad Pawar in 1999.

Article Title: HC judge vacancies at decade-low 26%, but pendency keeps piling up
Article Text:
Allahabad High Court

With 64 lakh cases, backlog refuses to ease

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: After hovering between 36% and 40% over the past decade, vacancies in HC judges have shown a significant decline, falling to 26%, this despite sanctioned strength of judges in HCs increasing from 906 in 2014 to 1,122.The largest HC, Allahabad, has brought down its vacancies to 56 against a sanctioned strength of 160 judges, as of Nov 1.The other HCs with bigger benches and usually large vacancies - Bombay, Punjab and Haryana, Madras, Calcutta, Karnataka and Delhi - too, have increased their working strength, bringing down vacancies.The last time judges' vacancies were this low (at 26%) was in July 2009, when there were 234 judges posts to be filled against a sanctioned strength of 886 in 21 HCs then.Vacancies in HCs started gradually climbing thereafter, which coincided with the friction between higher judiciary and govt over an attempt to bring a judicial accountability bill and passage of National Judicial Appointments Commission Act by Parliament. NJAC Act was later struck down by Supreme Court.In Nov 2014, vacancies were at 36% (in 24 HCs), with 353 judges posts vacant against a sanctioned strength of 984.These vacancies remained at 35% in March 2022 with 387 posts vacant, though the sanctioned strength was increased to 1,104 judges.Large vacancies are a prime factor behind backlog of cases. Though SC historically never had large vacancies, case pendency in SC has increased from 52,000 in 2009 to more than 92,000 at present.The situation is worse in HCs and much worse in district and lower judiciary, deteriorating every month. In 2009, total pendency of cases in HCs was at 39.5 lakh, which climbed to 45 lakh in 2013, and is at 64 lakh at present.The pendency in lower judiciary is similarly getting worse while the large number of vacancies remain static at around 5,000 against a sanctioned strength of 25,894 judicial officers.
Article Summary: Vacancies in HC judges have shown a significant decline, falling to 26%. This despite sanctioned strength of judges in HCs increasing from 906 in 2014 to 1,122. The last time judges' vacancies were this low (at 26%) was in July 2009.

CHENNAI: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has asked the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) to refuse certification to the Hindi film Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, starring Sunny Deol and Ravi Kishan, which is slated for release on Nov 20.The IMA objects to the film's teaser, released on Oct 19. In it, a father who has lost his daughter says doctors "write commission slips" instead of prescriptions, then asks how long people will tolerate this. The teaser then shows him assaulting doctors and nursing staff members inside a hospital, which the IMA says is presented as a heroic and justified act.In a representation dated Nov 4, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak urged the board to deny certification under Section 4(2)(v) read with Section 5B(1) of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, and the 2026 certification guidelines.The association said the objectionable content is the film's core theme and cannot be removed by mere excisions.The IMA wants the board to refuse certification to any trailer, teaser or promotional material that shows violence against doctors, nurses or hospital staff, or carries dialogue imputing corruption to doctors as a class.It has sought a screening under Section 7C for IMA representatives, the presence of an IMA-nominated medical expert when the examining committee views the film, and a hearing before any decision is taken.It said if any certificate is recommended, the chairperson should refer the film to a revising committee under Rule 25(1) of the Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 2024. It wants every scene showing violence against healthcare workers as justified or heroic deleted, along with the dialogue on corruption. It also wants a prominent disclaimer that the film does not represent the medical profession and that such violence is punishable.The association asked for a written, reasoned decision and priority consideration given the release date. It reserved the right to approach the courts.
Article Summary: The IMA objects to the film's teaser, released on Oct 19. In it, a father who has lost his daughter says doctors "write commission slips" instead of prescriptions. NEW DELHI: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge on Saturday accused the Central government of misleading people over ethanol blending in petrol, alleging that reports from government-accredited laboratories showed ethanol content exceeding the limits announced by the Centre.Kharge also alleged that the ethanol-blending programme was being used to benefit companies linked to the families of Union ministers. He claimed that some laboratory reports had indicated blending levels of up to 35-40 per cent, while others showed 31 per cent."The Government of India is lying through its teeth to the people. Very clearly, they had said that it (ethanol) will not be blended beyond a certain capacity, but NABL reports have proved that the ethanol blending is crossing the permissible limits, or at least the set limits that the govt had proclaimed. It's up to 35%, 40% in some cases. The lab reports are endorsed by laboratories that are accredited by the Govt of India," he said, as quoted by news agency ANI.The minister alleged that the policy was intended to facilitate certain companies. "This entire ethanol blending has been done only to facilitate companies of Union ministers," he said.Kharge's remarks came after Congress leader Rahul Gandhi accused the Centre of failing to disclose the actual ethanol content in petrol being sold across the country.In a post on X, the Congress MP said tests conducted on petrol samples collected from seven districts in Karnataka had found ethanol levels above the prescribed 20 per cent.He claimed that 11 of the 14 samples tested contained more than 20 per cent ethanol, with samples from Indian Oil Corporation (IOCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) recording 31.2 per cent and 30.5 per cent, respectively.Karnataka food, civil supplies, consumer affairs and legal metrology minister Rizwan Arshad had said the samples were collected from Bengaluru, Kolar, Chikkaballapura, Bengaluru Rural, Ramanagara, Mangaluru and Tumakuru. The tests were conducted by the NABL-accredited and ISO-certified Shriram Research Institute in Bengaluru.However, state-run oil marketing companies IOC, BPCL and HPCL have disputed the Karnataka government's findings. In a joint statement, the companies said E20 petrol supplied across their retail networks, including in Karnataka, complied with the Bureau of Indian Standards' IS 17021 specifications, which prescribe an ethanol content of 19-21 per cent.The companies also questioned the sampling and testing procedures used by the state government, saying the third-party laboratory certificates did not provide sufficient details of the testing methodology to independently verify the reported levels.Kharge referred to the Solicitor General's submission before the Supreme Court, in which ethanol blending was described as an experiment that was not being implemented across the country."If you recollect, the Solicitor General had told in the Supreme Court that this entire ethanol blending was an experiment and is not happening throughout the country, but if you actually look closely, you are experimenting on 1.3 billion people. How does that even work? So it is very clear that this Government of India has been lying to its own people only for profiteering," he said.He also cited the 31 per cent blending figure and referred to concerns raised by vehicle manufacturers over possible damage to vehicles."This is cheating the public, cheating being done for the company of a central minister's son. What is the NABL organisation saying? 31% blending is happening. They themselves are saying. Vehicle organisations have written letters saying vehicles are getting damaged; they have also threatened and intimidated, and got it withdrawn. Yesterday Rizwan Arshad spoke about NABL, where are BJP people now?" Kharge said.Rahul has also claimed that excessive ethanol blending could affect vehicle performance, leading to lower mileage and higher maintenance costs. He questioned the absence of labels at fuel stations disclosing the ethanol content of petrol.India's ethanol-blending programme began with a pilot initiative in 2001 and aims to reduce dependence on imported crude oil, strengthen domestic agricultural value chains and improve energy security.According to petroleum ministry data cited by the oil marketing companies, the programme has generated foreign exchange savings of more than Rs 1.97 lakh crore since the 2014-15 ethanol supply year, substituted around 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil and reduced carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 952 lakh metric tonnes.During the 2025-26 ethanol supply year, which ended on October 31, 2026, the three public sector oil marketing companies procured 1,089 crore litres of ethanol and blended 1,134 crore litres against petrol sales of around 5,673 crore litres.
Article Summary: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge accused the Central government of misleading people over ethanol blending in petrol. Kharge also alleged that the ethanol- blending programme was being used to benefit companies linked to the families of Union ministers. I tried very hard to fight the administration and also tried to talk to them about security... But today I have to embrace my own death because this Hemant Soren government can humiliate women, and I cannot bear this," she said.Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto said Bhagat had approached several people, including police officers, political representatives and social organisations, for help. He called for a comprehensive CBI investigation to establish whether complaints were ignored and identify those responsible.Her father, Handu Bhagat, also demanded a central investigation, alleging that influential people were involved. "I demand a high-level inquiry into my daughter's death. The probe should be conducted by the CBI, because high-profile people are involved," he told reporters.Ranchi Rural SP Gaurav Goswami said an Unnatural Death (UD) case had been registered and that forensic evidence had been collected from her residence. A medical board conducted the post-mortem examination."Everything is currently under investigation. We are looking into every point you have raised; however, it would be inappropriate to comment on any specific detail before the investigation is complete. Once the investigation concludes, all findings will be shared with you," Goswami said, responding to allegations of police negligence.Nisha Kumari Bhagat was a tribal activist from Jharkhand who had raised her voice against alleged injustice, starvation, religious conversion and land grabbing. She was particularly vocal against land brokers and what she described as harassment of tribal communities.According to Jharkhand BJP president Aditya Sahu, Bhagat had consistently spoken against exploitation and oppression but received no support from the government. He questioned why the police had failed to intervene despite thousands watching her distress broadcast.Union minister of state for Defence Sanjay Seth also accused the state administration of failing to act, demanding the arrest of the Pithoria police station officer-in-charge, whom Bhagat had allegedly accused of ignoring her complaints."The death of Nisha by suicide is a grim reflection of the crumbling law and order situation in Jharkhand," Seth said, reiterating the demand for a CBI probe.The case shares an eerie similarity to the killing of Bharat Bhushan Tiwari, whose death in a controversial police encounter in Bihar has sparked widespread outrage. A video apparently showing the 28-year-old activist throwing away his pistol moments before being shot has raised allegations that he was killed after surrendering. Amid mounting political pressure, the Bihar government had ordered a judicial inquiry led by a retired High Court judge and suspended four police personnel pending investigation.
Article Summary: Tribal activist Nisha Kumari Bhagat, who allegedly died by suicide, has triggered a political storm in Jharkhand. Opposition parties have accused the Hemant Soren-led government of failing to protect her despite repeated complaints of harassment. Her death has prompted the BJP to demand a CBI investigation and chief minister Soren's resignation.

Article Title: Cancer in India: Screening exists, but why are patients still diagnosed late
Article Text:
Offered, not taken: Why India still finds cancer late

A public programme that exists, and a habit that has not formed

What the national survey found

Why cancers are found late

Who should be screened, and when

Vaccination and cervical cancer

The barrier he names: Awareness

The urban and rural gap

The case for a yearly check-up

What it will take

Cancer in India is often detected late. By the time many patients are diagnosed, the disease has already advanced, when treatment is harder and the chances of survival are lower. Part of the explanation lies in how screening is organised in the country, and part lies in how people respond to early warning signs.The stakes are considerable. The Indian Council of Medical Research’s National Cancer Registry Programme estimated 13.92 lakh new cancer cases in India in 2020, up from 13.25 lakh in 2018, and about 7.7 lakh cancer deaths in 2020, according to figures the Union Health Ministry placed before Lok Sabha. The question that follows is how many of these cases could have been caught sooner.India does run a public screening system. The National Programme for Prevention and Control of Cancer, Diabetes, Cardiovascular Diseases and Stroke, now called the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD), was launched in 2010 in 100 districts across 21 states. In 2016, population-based screening was added for everyone aged 30 and above. It covers hypertension, diabetes and three cancers: of the oral cavity, the cervix and the breast.The design is meant to bring screening close to the community. Under the Health Ministry’s guidelines, an ASHA worker completes a Community Based Assessment Checklist. People aged 30 to 65 are then offered an oral visual examination and, for women, a clinical breast examination and a visual inspection of the cervix with acetic acid.Each is meant to be repeated once in five years. The ministry’s training module for staff nurses estimates that in a population of 1,000, about 370 people are eligible for oral cancer screening and about 182 women each for breast and cervical screening. The cervical test is offered at the primary health centre level to begin with.Uptake is low. The fifth National Family Health Survey, conducted between 2019 and 2021, asked adults aged 30 to 49 whether they had ever been screened for cancer. Among women, 1.9 per cent reported ever having had a cervical cancer screening test, 0.9 per cent a breast examination and 0.9 per cent an oral cavity examination. Among men, 1.2 per cent reported ever having had an oral cancer examination.The variation between states was wide. Tamil Nadu recorded the highest rates for cervical and breast screening, at 9.8 per cent and 5.6 per cent respectively. Cervical screening stood at 0.2 per cent in Gujarat, Assam and West Bengal, and in at least half of the states and Union Territories fewer than one per cent of women had ever been screened for it.Dr Prasad’s explanation has two parts. India has no mandatory screening programme, he said, and patients often ignore early signs, so they are diagnosed only when the disease is at an advanced stage.The Health Ministry’s 2016 operational framework for cancer screening makes the same point about late detection. It says cancers in India tend to be detected late, leaving little room for effective treatment, and cites five-year survival of 60.2, 76.3 and 73.2 per cent for early-stage oral, breast and cervical cancers, against 3.3, 14.9 and 7.9 per cent at an advanced stage. The figures come from a 2010 population-based study.The framework also stresses that screening is not an end in itself. It needs assured treatment, regular follow-up and linkages between every level of care, so that a person who tests positive can reach confirmation and treatment.Dr Prasad’s recommendations differ from what the public programme offers, and he set them out group by group.As per the guidelines, Dr Prasad said, women should begin breast cancer screening at 40. Women who are sexually active should be tested from 21, mainly to prevent cervical cancer. Men between 45 and 50 can have a Prostate Specific Antigen test once a year. Men and women alike should have a colonoscopy once every 10 years from the age of 50. From 40, he said, both men and women should mandatorily undergo a master health screening.The two differ in scope, age and frequency. The national framework’s screening protocols cover three cancers, oral, breast and cervical, for people aged 30 to 65, at five-year intervals; prostate and colorectal cancers are not among them. The framework itself notes that breast screening yields much more in women over 40, but keeps the starting age at 30 for programmatic and operational reasons.Dr Prasad also pointed to vaccination against cervical cancer for girls aged 9 to 14, which he said can prevent cervical cancer in women by up to 95 to 98 per cent. The Union Budget speech of February 2024 had announced that the government would encourage vaccination for girls in that age group.The national HPV vaccination campaign was launched in February 2026. It offers a free, voluntary, single-dose vaccine to 14-year-old girls, with parental consent, at government health facilities. The Health Ministry puts the annual cohort of 14-year-olds at about 1.2 crore girls, citing Registrar General of India estimates.By 11 September 2026, more than 80 lakh doses had been administered, the ministry said. Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Mizoram reported 100 per cent coverage of their identified target groups, while Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Assam had crossed 90 per cent. Uttar Pradesh had vaccinated more than 22 lakh girls, the highest of any state.Asked whether cost, fear, lack of awareness or access keeps people from being screened, Dr Prasad said it is mainly lack of awareness, along with the belief that nothing will happen to them. “Anything can happen to anyone at any point of time,” he said.The Health Ministry’s 2016 framework makes a related point. Because awareness of health is low, it says, screening for conditions with no obvious symptoms is seen as unnecessary, particularly among the poor, for whom a day’s visit to a secondary or tertiary facility can mean a lost day’s wages. On the cost of treatment, the Health Ministry has told Parliament that care in government hospitals is either free or highly subsidised for the poor and needy.In cities, Dr Prasad said, access and availability are plentiful, and a person with symptoms can reach cancer care. In tier two and tier three cities the best cancer care may not be available, he said, but screening is available in almost all government colleges and hospitals. Where tier one cities hold a clear advantage is awareness, because their residents have easier access to information about screening.The public cancer care network is meant to narrow the rest of the distance. Under the central government’s scheme for strengthening tertiary care for cancer, 19 State Cancer Institutes and 20 Tertiary Care Cancer Centres have been approved. The Centre and states share the cost in a 60:40 ratio, and 90:10 for the North-Eastern and hilly states, according to a reply in Rajya Sabha. In the Union Budget for 2025-26, the Finance Minister said the government would facilitate day-care cancer centres in all district hospitals over three years, with 200 to be set up in 2025-26.Asked for the one change that would do the most, Dr Prasad proposed mandatory health check-ups, once a year or at least once in two years, for everyone working in the government and private sectors.He expects the benefit to travel beyond the employee. This should also help in getting family members checked, he said, as many of them will come forward for testing. Cancer screening under the national programme, by comparison, is meant to be repeated once in five years.The pieces are not missing. A public programme offers screening for three cancers to people aged 30 to 65. A vaccination campaign is reaching 14-year-old girls through government facilities, and the Budget has announced day-care cancer centres for district hospitals. What the 2019–21 survey shows is a gap between what is offered and what people take up, with fewer than two in every hundred women aged 30 to 49 having ever been screened for cervical cancer.Dr Prasad’s account of that gap is a simple one: people do not think it can happen to them.
Article Summary: Cancer in India is often detected late, leaving little room for effective treatment. India has no mandatory screening programme, and patients often ignore early signs. Tamil Nadu recorded the highest rates for cervical and breast screening. Cervical screening stood at 0.2 per cent in Gujarat, Assam and West Bengal.

Article Title: PG doctors quit premier medical institutes
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Postgraduate doctors are walking away from residency programmes at some of India's leading medical institutions. RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and JIPMER , with AIIMS Delhi alone reporting 34 junior resident departures in 2025.While several institutes lack consolidated data on psychiatric counselling or workplace stress among residents, Dr Lakshya Mittal, chairperson of United Doctors Front (UDF), said multiple RTI applications filed by its members had revealed postgraduate doctors quitting premier medical institutions despite securing top NEET-PG ranks. He cited complaints of duties extending beyond 36 hours, workplace harassment, toxic work culture and inadequate support.“Residency is meant to train doctors, not break them. Discipline is not humiliation and dedication is not exploitation,” Mittal said, urging authorities to enforce working-hour regulations, establish independent grievance-redressal mechanisms and fix institutional accountability. UDF has also filed a PIL in the Supreme Court.However, the figures from individual institutions show that departures have continued, even as some reported a decline.At AIIMS Delhi, 34 junior resident doctors quit in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a decline of about 43%. The number of residents joining also fell, from 324 in 2024 to 267 in 2025. Department-wise figures show the highest number of exits in anaesthesiology at seven, followed by ophthalmology at six. Surgery reported three exits, as did pathology. Ophthalmology had recorded 14 exits in 2024.JIPMER, Puducherry, also reported a decline in resignations. A combined count of departures from its January and July batches shows 44 residents resigned in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a fall of nearly 27%. However, exits continued across several specialities, including anaesthesiology, emergency medicine, orthopaedics, pathology and surgery.The trend is not confined to these two institutions. AIIMS Kalyani reported 15 exits across all three years of postgraduate training in 2025, including 13 from the January and July batches. Another 11 students from the 2026 batches had left by the time of its reply. AIIMS Raipur reported 19 exits from its 2025 batches, AIIMS Patna 12, while AIIMS Gorakhpur also reported departures. At AIIMS Rishikesh, 30 students across various postgraduate and super-speciality programmes left in 2025.The RTI also sought details of psychiatric counselling and whether stress, depression or sleep deprivation were recorded as reasons for leaving. AIIMS Delhi said it had no compiled counselling data, while AIIMS Rishikesh reported six postgraduate students receiving psychiatric counselling in 2026 but maintained no consolidated record of workplace-related stress. AIIMS Raipur reported no residents seeking counselling in 2025 or 2026.AIIMS Patna reported 15 residents receiving counselling in 2025 and none in 2026, while AIIMS Kalyani declined to provide the information, citing RTI provisions.The figures are not directly comparable as institutes provided data for different periods and batches. While they establish that residents are leaving, the reasons remain unclear, with several institutes lacking records that could help explain the departures.
Article Summary: Postgraduate doctors are walking away from residency programmes at some of India's leading medical institutions. RTI replies show exits across AIIMS campuses and JIPMER. At AIIMs Delhi, 34 junior resident doctors quit in 2025, compared with 60 in 2024, a decline of about 43%. exits continued across several specialities, including anaesthesiology.

Article Title: Massive anti-drug drive: 458 acres of illicit cannabis eradicated in Arunachal Pradesh
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a major crackdown on drug production, the Narcotics Control Bureau’s Itanagar Zonal Unit, operating alongside the Sashastra Seema Bal, Central Reserve Police Force, and Arunachal Pradesh Police, has eradicated approximately 458 acres of illicit cannabis cultivation in the Kalaktang subdivision of West Kameng district.The first phase of the joint destruction operation, carried out between October 26 and November 3, 2026, resulted in the destruction of over 1.37 lakh kilograms of cannabis plants grown primarily on community lands.The drive mobilized 118 personnel and workers, drawing enforcement officers from the Sashastra Seema Bal, Central Reserve Police Force, Arunachal Pradesh Anti-Narcotics Task Force, West Kameng Police, and the district administration. Ground surveys conducted by local police and civil authorities, paired with satellite mapping provided by the NCB, allowed field teams to pinpoint and access illegal plantation sites hidden deep within the region's rugged terrain.With this latest action, the total area of illicit cannabis destroyed across Arunachal Pradesh in 2026 has surged to more than eight times the full-year figure recorded in 2025.The operation forms part of a broader crackdown mapped out under the Vision Document on Narcotics Control (2026–2029), which mandates identifying cultivation hotspots and executing synchronized crop destruction operations using a whole-of-government approach across central, state, and district agencies.NCB authorities confirmed that further joint drives are scheduled to target illicit cannabis and opium poppy sites identified across the state, including high-risk opium regions in Lohit, Lower Dibang Valley, Dibang Valley, Namsai, Anjaw, Tirap, Changlang, and Longding.The Arunachal Pradesh drive follows similar nationwide operations led by the agency, including the clearance of nearly 592 acres of illegal cannabis in Himachal Pradesh's Parvati Valley in Kullu, as well as joint operations under Odisha's Mission Zero Cannabis Cultivation, which recently saw 30 acres destroyed in Kandhamal district.Authorities continue to urge members of the public to report illicit drug cultivation or trafficking activities confidentially through the toll-free MANAS National Narcotics Helpline at 1933.
Article Summary: Narcotics Control Bureau's Itanagar Zonal Unit has eradicated 458 acres of illicit cannabis cultivation in the Kalaktang subdivision of West Kameng district. The drive mobilized 118 personnel and workers, drawing enforcement officers from the Sashastra Seema Bal, Central Reserve Police Force, and Arunachal Pradesh Police.

NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar was discharged from Mumbai's Breach Candy Hospital on Saturday after receiving treatment for a bronchitis attack and chest infection, with his doctor confirming that the veteran politician was in a stable condition and would continue his recovery at home.Providing an update on Pawar's health, Dr Pritam Samdani said the 85-year-old was responding well to treatment and that his condition had improved. He added that Pawar had been advised to continue medication and follow additional precautions given his age."Sharad Pawar has been discharged in a stable condition . He will continue his treatment at home... He had suffered from a bronchitis attack and a chest infection, which are now improving... He has been asked to continue his treatment at home and to take standard precautions that every citizen of the country should take... Given his age, a few additional instructions have been provided. However, he was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai the same day for further treatment.He had remained under medical observation at the hospital for the past three days.Earlier, Maharashtra deputy chief inister Eknath Shinde had visited Pawar at the hospital to enquire about his health. Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Shinde said the NCP (SP) chief was recovering well and that all his medical parameters were normal.Also read: Miffed with Parth, NCP seniors eager to revive merger talks with Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP); surprised, says Rohit Shinde also said that despite being hospitalised, Pawar had discussed issues concerning farmers, drought-hit areas and water shortages in parts of Maharashtra, including Satara and Mahabaleshwar.Several political leaders and prominent personalities had also visited the veteran leader during his hospitalisation. Article Title: ‘Relief to breathe Kerala’s clean air’: Shashi Tharoor takes swipe at Delhi govt over pollution crisis
Article Text:
Tharoor questioned why the Centre and the governments of Delhi and Haryana had not taken concrete steps to tackle the crisis

GRAP 3 imposed

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Saturday criticised the governments at the Centre and in Delhi, Haryana and Punjab over the worsening air pollution crisis, saying they must work together and show the political will to take concrete action.Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, Tharoor said the current political situation offered an opportunity for governments to coordinate, as the Centre and the three states were not governed by the Congress.“The government must find the political will to act. I wrote an article some months ago saying that this is an unusual situation now, where the Central Government, the Delhi Government, the Haryana Government and the Punjab Government can all be on the same page. None of them is Congress. You don't have to blame us. They can sit together and make a plan,” he said.Tharoor questioned why the Centre and the governments of Delhi and Haryana had not taken concrete steps to tackle the crisis, alleging that the situation was being allowed to spiral out of control.“At least Haryana, Delhi and the Centre, why can't they do something concrete about air pollution? They are allowing this to get completely out of control,” he said.Taking a dig at the pollution levels in the national capital, the Congress leader said it was a relief to breathe Kerala's clean air instead of being in Delhi's polluted atmosphere.“It is a relief to breathe the clean air of Kerala rather than be in the absolutely polluted atmosphere of Delhi,” Tharoor added.Delhi's air pollution control measures were tightened with the implementation of Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) on Friday, as the city's air quality deteriorated towards the severe category.The average Air Quality Index (AQI) stood at 382 at 4pm on Friday, up from 369 a day earlier. The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) invoked GRAP Stage III as a precautionary measure, just four days after Stage II restrictions came into force.Under GRAP Stage III, major dust-generating construction and demolition activities are prohibited, while stone crushers and mining operations are required to shut down. Restrictions also apply to BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel cars in Delhi and five high-vehicle-density districts of the National Capital Region.The measures also include the possibility of hybrid classes for students up to Class V and a 50% work-from-home arrangement in offices.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor criticised the governments at the Centre and in Delhi, Haryana and Punjab over the worsening air pollution crisis. He said they must work together and show the political will to take concrete action. The average Air Quality Index stood at 382 at 4pm on Friday, up from 369 a day earlier.
